stage1.impression: This reads as an architectural CG street, not a night photograph. The neighbouring walls carry a flat procedural cloud texture, and their windows are either flat saturated blue panes or empty black voids. The bay windows above are the brightest thing in the frame, while the shopfront, which is the subject, sits darker than everything around it. The lightbox dancer and the warm room behind the glass are lovely ideas, but at this size and exposure they are a small dim postcard in a big blue set, and no EARF speaker reads at a glance. As it stands a magazine would not run it as a specific place: it looks like a generic render of a street, with only the lightbox and the etched name hinting at a particular bar.

blocking_9: The shopfront must be the brightest and warmest zone in the frame: shopfront region [400,330,900,665] lum_median above the neighbouring facades [0,0,390,610] and [905,0,1200,680], not 27.5 against 68 to 80.

The neighbouring facades need real material at 1:1 (stucco or brick with joints, sills, staining and downpipes), not a uniform cloud noise. Their windows need believable interiors (curtains, a lamp, a dark room with reflections), not flat #0040B0-like blue panes and pure black voids.

The room behind the glass must be legible as a listening bar from across the street: the window interior [540,440,715,600] at lum_median 45 or more, with the counter, a pool of light and ideally one smoked Atmosphere speaker or Dome readable through the glass.
Some sign of life on the street or in the room: a figure at the counter or in the doorway, a bike, a parked car edge, a menu board.
The wet street reflection needs texture (asphalt grain, puddle edges, a kerb with wear), not one smooth mirror sheet.

defects.what: Neighbour facade is a uniform procedural cloud texture with no joints, staining, sills or scale cues; reads as CG.
Right neighbour facade shows the same cloud texture and is brighter (median 80.5) than the subject shopfront.
Upper windows are flat saturated blue panes (r_median 1, b_median 97), which reads as emissive game glass. They also add a second saturated colour to the frame.
Big black void window on the left neighbour (crush_pct 60.7) next to a single repeated roller blind; reads as an empty box.
Second black void window on the right neighbour, with no reflection or interior.
Bay window blinds are the brightest surfaces in the frame (median 86, p95 148), flat grey and uniformly lit; they pull the eye away from the shopfront.
The same striped blind model repeats in several windows (repeated asset).
Room behind the glass is underexposed (median 23.4) and small in frame; the speakers and the counter do not read.
The etched EARF name reads as flat pale block letters floating in the glass rather than an etched, frosted glass mark.
The entrance vestibule is murky (median 26.4). The blackened steel shows blotchy smeared patina at 1:1 (denoiser and texture smear), and the vestibule floor is a flat bright slab.
Street and pavement are a smooth blue sheet with mirror reflection and no asphalt grain, kerb wear or puddle edges.
Transom glass band reads as flat dark panels with faint strip highlights, with no depth.

changes.problem: The exposure hierarchy is inverted: the blue-hour ambient lights the neighbours and the bays more than the room lights the shopfront.

evidence.measured: shopfront lum_median 27.5 against left facade 67.9, right facade 80.5 and bays 86.3

change.to: about 0.4x current, so the facades sit at median 30 to 40 and keep a deep blue-hour tone

changes.expected: Facades drop to median 30 to 40 and the lit shopfront becomes the brightest block in the frame.

changes.problem: The room behind the glass is too dim to read from across the street.

change.setting: the Domes' downlights; record wall spots; exposure
change.from: Domes 260 W, record wall 30 W, exposure 1.8
change.to: Domes 450 W, record wall 60 W, and exposure 2.2 once c1 has lowered the ambient

changes.expected: Warm pools on the counter and record wall read through the glass, and the interior median rises to about 50 with practicals still unclipped.

changes.problem: From 12.5 m at 35 mm the shopfront fills only about 40 % of the width, so the frame is mostly generic neighbour wall and the speaker and room cannot read.

evidence.measured: subject spans about 500 of 1200 px; upper half of frame is facades and bays

changes.problem: The neighbour facades use a cloud-noise texture with no scale, which says CG at first glance.

evidence.measured: uniform mottling across 390x610 px, with no joints, sills or staining

change.to: painted stucco or brick with mortar joints at real scale, window sills, drip staining under sills, a downpipe, and a lower plinth band at street level

changes.expected: The facades read as real San Francisco buildings, and the eye has structure that leads to the shopfront.

changes.problem: The neighbour windows are flat saturated blue panes or black voids, adding a second colour and an empty-box feel.

change.setting: neighbour window glass and interiors (plain description)
change.from: flat blue reflective panes and black voids [60,440,370,595] crush 60.7 %
change.to: glass reflecting the actual sky with curtains or blinds behind; one or two windows warm-lit at low level (2700 K, dim); the ground-floor black voids given a dim interior or a roller shutter

changes.expected: No pure saturated blue in the windows; the frame's colour comes from the warm room and its smoked products.

changes.problem: The bay blinds above are the brightest surfaces and pull the eye up and away from the bar.

change.setting: bay window blinds (plain description) plus the ambient change in c1
change.to: darker blinds with one bay dimly warm-lit from inside, so the flats feel inhabited

changes.expected: The bays sit about 1 stop below the shopfront and stop competing with it.

changes.problem: There is no sign of life, so the scene reads as a showroom set.

evidence.measured: no figures, bikes or street objects anywhere in the frame

change.to: a figure at the counter seen through the glass, a bicycle against the pier at right of the door, and a small A-board or the brass coin bowl visible at the door

changes.expected: Scale and life: a reader takes it as a working bar at opening time.

changes.problem: The street is a smooth mirror sheet, and the steel shopfront shows blotchy smear at 1:1.

evidence.measured: lum_range only 53.3 across the whole street band; smooth blue gradient with mirror reflections

change.from: glossy uniform street; blotchy steel texture
change.to: asphalt roughness about 0.35 with a roughness mask for puddles, a worn concrete kerb; the steel's patina scale reduced to fine, even brushing with sharp edges; street lamps raised from 200 W to 350 W at 3000 K for warm pools on the pavement

changes.expected: Broken, believable reflections and warm pools on the pavement that tie the street to the warm shopfront.

out_of_scope.request: Make a smoked Atmosphere speaker clearly visible through the shopfront glass as the colour hero.
out_of_scope.why: Where the speakers sit is fixed by the room's design. Only the camera (c3) and the lighting (c2) can bring one into view; if none is in line of sight, the owner must decide whether this frame needs one.

out_of_scope.request: Make the etched name read as etched frosted glass rather than flat pale letters.
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront design is fixed. Only the etched name's emission (0.04) can be tuned; a change to the etching's material or form is a design change.
